09.1.new:
Limits: see section 17.
- A JUDGMENT'S OWN DISAGREEMENTS GO TO THE JUDGE AT THE LATE GATE (ASK 624.5; Shared Library entry SCK624, read by `P Late Gate Build` and `P Gate Record` on each path P, the panel, Alt and R2 Alt; the child takes the text in the call; no prompt and no instruction to a judge is changed):
  - What is checked: each counted judge's text as it stands after the send-back and gate changes are applied, with the engine's recomputed verdict word. Three kinds of item, each naming two of the judge's own lines:
    1. WHICH HOLDS AGREEMENT: WHICH HOLDS: CHALLENGER with a verdict other than BROKEN, or WHICH HOLDS: DEFENDER with BROKEN (the reading of WHL507). The item reads: "Your WHICH HOLDS line and your verdict do not agree. Your WHICH HOLDS line: \"<line>\". Your verdict after the gate: <word>, and your RESULT line: \"<line>\". WHICH HOLDS: CHALLENGER goes with BROKEN; WHICH HOLDS: DEFENDER goes with HELD or PARTIAL. CHANGE TO the one line you hold wrong, or KEEP with the words that decide it."
    2. RETRACTION LEFT STANDING: a line "RETRACTED: Dn vs Cm" stands, and another line still rests on that pair: a pair line that grades it DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or BROKEN; a CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS line that names a verse of that pair's line; or a line reading "Dn is broken" or "broken at Dn" when no other pair of Dn that is not retracted is graded broken against the defender. The item reads: "You retracted <Dn vs Cm>, and a line of yours still rests on it. Your retraction: \"<line>\". Your line: \"<line>\". CHANGE TO that line so it no longer rests on <Dn vs Cm>, or KEEP with the words that decide it."
    3. TWO GRADES: one pair carries two different grades in "Dn vs Cm (ref): GRADE" form (the first reading of pkgGCA); AUDIT and EXTRACTOR lines and STANDING, RETRACTED, STATEMENT and PRESSED lines are set aside. The item reads: "You give <Dn vs Cm> two different grades. Your line: \"<line 1>\". Your other line: \"<line 2>\". CHANGE TO the one line you hold wrong, or KEEP with the words that decide it."
    No item says which line, which reading or which side is right; the judge chooses which line changes (ruling 428).
  - What is sent: every item of kinds 1 and 3, and an item of kind 2 whose resting line is a pair line or a CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS line. Each sent item ends "A KEEP does not cure this item." A kind 2 item whose resting line is a ruling line (the "is broken" or "broken at" reading) is recorded and not sent, because the change-apply step cannot replace that line. The late gate sends its message also when these items are the only late items. They take G numbers with the other late items and are shown "ITEM G<n> (SELF-CHECK; <kind>):". When they are present the message says: "Lines of your judgment disagree with each other (the item(s) marked SELF-CHECK below); you choose which line changes." and "A SELF-CHECK item left uncured counts against your seat once."
  - The change: a CHANGE TO a whole WHICH HOLDS line is a line form the engine reads and replaces the judge's WHICH HOLDS line; this holds wherever the change-apply step (`sbApply2024`) runs, the send-back and the gate included. RESULT and pair lines are applied as before.
  - The cure: the self-check items are kept out of the gate's cure reading. A CHANGE is applied with the other changes and the check is run again on the result: the item is CURED only if the change was made and the check no longer raises it. A KEEP, no answer, or a change that leaves the disagreement is UNCURED and adds 1 to `drv_uncured`, so it can remove the seat.
  - Records: one `debate_enforcer_log` row per item, rule E-SCK, item "SELF-CHECK G<n> <kind>", its flagged_line the two lines; the audit line "[AUDIT v60: SELF-CHECK (ASK 624.5) -- SEAT: ...". An item not sent is written "[AUDIT v60: SELF-CHECK RECORD ONLY (ASK 624.5) -- SEAT: <seat>; <kind>: <item text> NOT SENT: no apply path for this line.]". A fault of the check itself is written "[AUDIT v60: SELF-CHECK FAULT (ASK 624.5) -- SEAT: <seat>; the self-check threw and was not run: <error>. REVIEW THIS ROW.]" and sends nothing.
  - Unchanged: the E-WHL rows of Send Back Build stay a trial and are not sent there, because the gate may still change the text; the pkgGCA audit line of Alternate Merge is still written.
  - Shown offline: of twelve stored judgments one has items, judgment 1276 (chatgpt, run 42373): three sent, one of each kind, and two recorded only; the other eleven send none. A WHICH HOLDS change is applied and the second check clears it; a KEEP stays open; an applied change that still disagrees stays open. Not shown by a run. Limits: a judge that does not answer the item in form loses the count for it, so the check can cost a seat without changing a verdict. Marks: an E-SCK row that is sent and answered; no stored judgment whose engine word names one side beside a WHICH HOLDS line for the other.
- THE ENFORCER (TRIAL; md_notes_rulings 421, 424; the enforcer model is luna):

11.0.old: A judge whose finding contradicts its own grades is not sent back, and nothing yet makes them agree (the send-back apply path reads no WHICH HOLDS line).
11.0.new: At this stage a judge whose finding contradicts its own grades is not sent back. A WHICH HOLDS line that disagrees with the verdict after the gate is sent at the late gate, and a CHANGE TO a WHICH HOLDS line is applied (A JUDGMENT'S OWN DISAGREEMENTS GO TO THE JUDGE AT THE LATE GATE, section 9).
